lesson.title: Comparison Gym
lesson.subtitle: plus… que, moins… que, aussi… que across cities, food, and ideas.

hook.title: Running Comparisons at Speed: plus… que, moins… que, aussi… que
hook.content: Run the three comparison frames across adjectives you own: plus [adj] que ('more [adj] than'), moins [adj] que ('less [adj] than'), and aussi [adj] que ('as [adj] as'). The adjective still agrees in gender and number with the subject being described!

footnotes.title: When the final -s of plus wakes up
footnotes.content: Before a consonant (plus grand, plus cher), the -s of plus is silent (/ply/). Before a vowel (plus‿important), the -s wakes up in liaison as /z/!

pattern.title: Subject + être + plus/moins/aussi + Agreed Adjective + que + Target
pattern.content: Keep the adjective agreed with the first noun, and close every comparison with que.
pattern.linguist_note: Comparative degree markers precede the adjective while the standard of comparison is introduced by que.
pattern.trap_note: Don't use *comme after aussi in a comparison (*aussi grand comme) — even for 'as... as', the second word is que (aussi grand que)!

exercises.prompt: Match each comparative sentence with its meaning:

matching_pairs.english: La maison est plus grande que l'hôtel
matching_pairs.german: The house is bigger than the hotel

matching_pairs.english: Le train est moins cher que l'avion
matching_pairs.german: The train is cheaper than the plane

matching_pairs.english: Lyon est aussi beau que Paris
matching_pairs.german: Lyon is as beautiful as Paris

matching_pairs.english: Cette table est plus petite que l'autre
matching_pairs.german: This table is smaller than the other

exercises.target_answer: The house is bigger than the hotel, The train is cheaper than the plane, Lyon is as beautiful as Paris, This table is smaller than the other
exercises.meaning: La maison est plus grande que l'hôtel, Le train est moins cher que l'avion, Lyon est aussi beau que Paris, Cette table est plus petite que l'autre
exercises.explanation: All three frames (plus, moins, aussi) close with que.

exercises.prompt: How do you say 'She is as tall as her brother'?
options: Elle est aussi grande que son frère
Elle est aussi grande comme son frère
Elle est aussi grand que son frère
exercises.target_answer: Elle est aussi grande que son frère
exercises.meaning: She is as tall as her brother
exercises.explanation: grande agrees with Elle (-e), and 'as... as' uses aussi... que!

exercises.prompt: What is the word-for-word structure of 'Le train est moins cher que le taxi'?
exercises.german: Le train est moins cher que le taxi
exercises.natural: The train is cheaper than the taxi
options: The train is cheaper than the taxi
The train is less dear than the taxi
The train is fewer expensive as the taxi
exercises.target_answer: The train is less dear than the taxi
exercises.meaning: Literal structure: The train is less dear than the taxi

exercises.idea: this city is bigger than my city
cues: This city is bigger → Cette ville est plus grande
than my city → que ma ville
idea_parts: subject + comparative → Cette ville est plus grande
exercises.target_answer: Cette ville est plus grande que ma ville
exercises.meaning: This city is bigger than my city
exercises.explanation: la ville is feminine, so grande takes -e.

diagnosis.cue: ville is feminine: plus grande que ma ville.

exercises.prompt: Listen and write the whole sentence.
exercises.spoken: C'est moins compliqué que je pensais
exercises.target_answer: C'est moins compliqué que je pensais
exercises.meaning: It is less complicated than I thought
exercises.explanation: moins... que works with clauses too!
exercises.affirmation: You wrote moins compliqué que je pensais cleanly.

summary.outcome: Compare people, places, and things using plus… que, moins… que, and aussi… que with full adjective agreement.

use_example.german: Ce bistro est moins cher et aussi bon que le restaurant.
use_example.english: This bistro is cheaper and just as good as the restaurant.

summary.takeaway: 'as... as' is aussi... que (never comme), and the adjective agrees with the first noun.
summary.curiosity_teaser: Up next on Le Pont ([22] en & y): see how Comparison Gym leads directly into en & y.

twist.prompt: Think it through again without looking back — express "This city is bigger than my city" in French:
twist.target_answer: Cette ville est plus grande que ma ville
twist.explanation: Re-constructing "Cette ville est plus grande que ma ville" from the underlying rule cements the pattern of Comparison Gym.

plus.etymology_derivation: borrowed into English whole — plus is plus. The final s falls silent in most positions.

aussi.context_phrase: Elle est aussi grande que son frère.
aussi.context_translation: She is as tall as her brother.
aussi.etymology_derivation: Inside comparisons, aussi + adjective + que means 'as [adj] as'.

que.context_phrase: Paris est plus grand que Lyon.

grand.etymology_derivation: English 'grand' came straight from French; the feminine adds a silent -e, which wakes the silent d into sound: grand /ɡʁɑ̃/ → grande /ɡʁɑ̃d/.

petit.etymology_derivation: English 'petite' is the French feminine form, borrowed whole — the masculine is petit.

ville.etymology_derivation: Latin vīlla 'country estate' grew into the whole city in French (leaving 'city' as la cité for the historic core).

hôtel.shift_rule: Norman doublet: S and H dropped
hôtel.etymology_derivation: Latin hospitalis → hostel AND hôtel — the same word entered English twice: once with its S (hostel, hospital), once without (hôtel).
